duration: One year or until specific land-use standards were developed, whichever occurred first
legal_basis: Ordinance 1515, "An Ordinance Imposing a Temporary Moratorium on Data Centers and Crypto Mining Facilities in the City of Harrison, Arkansas"
trigger: Green Digital conditional-use application; Arkansas Data Centers Act of 2023; zoning code did not list data centers or crypto mining facilities; concerns over electricity use, greenhouse gas emissions, pollution, e-waste, noise, and local impacts
current_status: Repealed; Harrison City Council voted 6-2 to repeal Ordinance 1515 at a specially called meeting on Tuesday, 2023-11-28, on a motion by Council Member Mitch Magness, seconded by Council Member Joel Williams (councilors Jeremy Ragland and Wayne Cone voted no). City Attorney Nancy Cartwright recommended repeal as a litigation precaution tied to a federal court matter involving Green Digital and the state's data-mining protections; the council also amended its noise ordinance the same night (Ordinance 1516). No separate numbered repeal ordinance for Ordinance 1515 itself was identified in the Harrison Daily Times' contemporaneous account of the meeting, and the city's own ordinance/clerk portal (harrisonar.gov) is behind a bot-protection challenge page that could not be bypassed to check the clerk's ordinance index directly.
affected_projects: Green Digital / Metahash crypto-mining data center; Chamber timeline reports a 10 MW Entergy contract and estimated $2.5 million capital investment
outcome: Moratorium was removed after officials concluded it increased legal exposure under the state "right to mine" framework; later state Acts 173 and 174 of 2024 restored more local and state regulatory authority over crypto mining

date_enacted: 2026-07-16 (City Council amended a proposed 18-month moratorium to six months by a 6-2 vote, then adopted the amended ordinance by another 6-2 vote)
duration: Six-month moratorium as amended and adopted; originally proposed as an 18-month moratorium in a June 16, 2026 councilmember proposal
legal_basis: City Council ordinance (instrument number not confirmed); creates a temporary committee to recommend regulations
trigger: Pause on acceptance, processing, and approval of applications for data center development, construction, or siting within city limits; officials said no active data center proposal was known
current_status: Active as of 2026-09-23. The July 16, 2026 City Council agenda (Item 3, New Business) confirms the ordinance considered and adopted that night was titled 'An Ordinance Imposing a Temporary Moratorium on the Acceptance, Processing and Approval of Applications for the Development, Construction, or Siting of Data Centers Within the Incorporated Areas of the City of Russellville... Establishing a Temporary Committee...', sponsored by Council Member Justin Keller; River Valley Radio and a Citizen Portal meeting summary confirm the council amended the sponsor's original 18-month proposal down to six months (6-2) and then adopted the amended ordinance (6-2). The resulting ad hoc committee (also reported as the 'Data Center Research Committee' / 'Zoning and Land Use Amendments Committee') was seated and was still actively meeting as of an Aug. 18, 2026 River Valley Radio report, with no report found of the moratorium being lifted or repealed early. The signed ordinance's assigned number, precise effective date, and sunset date still were not located in the city's online ordinance archive or on Municode as of 2026-09-23.
